tagline: Up into dry mountains and very old wood.
intro: From Big Pine, Route 168 climbs into the White Mountains through Westgard Pass, and White Mountain Road leads on into the bristlecone country. These are arid mountains. Living pines more than four thousand years old grow here, their weathered, twisted wood set above views into Nevada's Great Basin.
Schulman Grove has the visitor center, open in summer. Beyond it the road turns to dirt for Patriarch Grove, and the Forest Service says both groves can be seen in one day with an early start.

moments.title: Schulman Grove
moments.text: Bristlecones stand within view of the parking area and the boardwalks around the visitor center, and self-guided trails lead farther in.

moments.title: Patriarch Grove
moments.text: Thirteen miles of dirt road end at a remote grove with a moonscape look, home of the Patriarch Tree, where two short trails wander among the pines.

practical: The road beyond Schulman Grove to Patriarch Grove is dirt, there is no water in the forest, and the nearest food, water or fuel is in Big Pine.
